candidates.title: A session can adopt an existing device id with new keys and get it auto-approved, bypassing device approval
trace: server/src/devices.js GET /api/devices lists all device ids to any session
devices.js PUT /api/devices/current: deviceId = user.deviceId ?? body.device_id, no proof of the old key
autoApprove counts approved devices excluding the one being re-keyed -> 0 on a single-device account
keys overwritten, approved_at = now(), contacts fetch the attacker's keys
candidates.fix: Require proof of the old signing key to adopt a device id; never auto-approve a re-key of an existing device.

candidates.title: One account can fill Redis through the relay queue (self-relay, 2000 x 128 KB per device) and take the service down
trace: devices.js POST /api/relay: self-relay needs no contact
envelope up to 128 KB, queue cap 2000 messages, device ids not deduped
candidates.fix: Byte budget per recipient device and per sender; dedupe device ids.

candidates.title: Same as U1-2 (revoked sessions keep WebSockets)

hardening_notes: approve UPDATE doesn't re-check the keys the signature covered (TOCTOU)
de-approval by key change doesn't refresh the device cache or open sockets
PUT push token clears that token from any user's device
contacts can drain each other's one-time prekeys at 60/min
